# Base image for the build
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments, allowing root execution
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1

# Install dependencies, build applications, and clean up in a single layer
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    && mkdir -p /build && cd /build \
    #
    # --- Build and install METIS 4.0.3 ---
    #
    && wget -O metis-4.0.3.tar.gz https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz \
    && tar -xvzf metis-4.0.3.tar.gz \
    && cd metis-4.0.3 \
    && make OPTFLAGS='-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration' \
    && cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ \
    && cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/include/ \
    && cd .. \
    #
    # --- Build and install HYPRE 2.28.0 ---
    #
    && wget -O hypre-2.28.0.tar.gz https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/refs/tags/v2.28.0.tar.gz \
    && tar -xvzf hypre-2.28.0.tar.gz \
    && cd hypre-2.28.0/src \
    && ./configure --prefix=/usr/local --disable-fortran --enable-bigint \
    && make -j$(nproc) \
    && make install \
    && cd ../.. \
    #
    # --- Build MFEM 4.7 ---
    #
    && git clone --depth 1 --branch v4.7 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git \
    && cd mfem \
    && make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_METIS_4=YES HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local MFEM_USE_MPI=YES CXX=mpic++ \
    && cd .. \
    #
    # --- Build Laghos and install executable ---
    #
    && git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git \
    && cd Laghos \
    # FIX: Point MFEM_DIR to the relative mfem build directory instead of a system-wide install path.
    && make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=../mfem \
    && cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ \
    #
    # --- Set up final working directory and copy data files ---
    #
    && mkdir -p /app \
    && cp -r data/* /app/ \
    && cd / \
    #
    # --- Clean up build directory and apt cache ---
    #
    && rm -rf /build \
    && apt-get clean \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set the final working directory
WORKDIR /app

# This MiniCluster manifest defines a single-node, multi-task Flux job
# to run the Laghos HPC application on an AWS CPU instance in Kubernetes.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster job.
  name: laghos-aws-cpu-experiment
  # Deploy to the 'default' namespace.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # Size defines the number of pods for the MiniCluster.
  # A size of 1 indicates a single-node execution environment.
  size: 1

  # Tasks specifies the total number of MPI ranks for the job.
  # Flux will start 4 processes of the 'laghos' application inside the pod.
  tasks: 4

  # By setting cleanup to false, the completed job pods and their logs
  # will be retained for inspection after the run completes.
  cleanup: false

  # Logging settings for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict schema validation for the MiniCluster spec.
    strict: true

  # The containers list defines the application and any sidecars.
  # For this HPC job, we only need one container.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:laghos
      
      # The command to be executed by `flux run -n <tasks>`.
      # Note: Do not include `flux run` or `mpirun` in the command.
      # The command runs laghos with the specified mesh file and common parameters for a test run.
      command: laghos -p 1 -m cube_311_hex.mesh -r 2 -t 2 -tf 0.6
      
      # The launcher flag must be false for the primary application container.
      # The Flux Operator manages the launch process.
      launcher: false

      # Sets the working directory inside the container.
      # This ensures 'laghos' is executed in the directory containing the mesh file.
      workingDir: /opt/laghos/data

# This corrected MiniCluster manifest incorporates feedback to fix the application execution.
# It adheres strictly to the original constraints, avoiding unsupported or disallowed fields.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster job.
  name: laghos-aws-cpu-experiment
  # Deploy to the 'default' namespace.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # Size defines the number of pods for the MiniCluster.
  # A size of 1 indicates a single-node execution environment as requested.
  size: 1

  # Tasks specifies the total number of MPI ranks for the job.
  # Flux will start 4 processes of the 'laghos' application inside the pod.
  tasks: 4

  # By setting cleanup to false, the completed job pods and their logs
  # will be retained for inspection after the run completes.
  cleanup: false

  # Logging settings for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict schema validation for the MiniCluster spec.
    strict: true

  # The containers list defines the application.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:laghos
      
      # Corrected command to be executed by `flux run`.
      # FIX: Replaced invalid `-r` flag with the correct `-rs` for serial refinement.
      # FIX: Added `-f` to output the Figure of Merit (FOM) for performance measurement.
      command: laghos -p 1 -m cube_311_hex.mesh -rs 2 -tf 0.6 -f
      
      # The launcher flag must be false for the primary application container.
      launcher: false

      # Sets the working directory inside the container.
      # FIX: Changed working directory to `/app` where the application and data files are located.
      workingDir: /app

import math
from typing import Dict, Any, Literal
import json

def evaluate_laghos_run(
    total_elements: int,
    total_ranks: int,
    nodes_used: int,
    cores_per_node: int,
    memory_gb_per_node: int,
    threading_hint: int,
    current_fom: float,
    threshold: float = 0.90,
    ideal_fom_per_core: float = 1.5e6,
    efficiency_sweet_spot: float = 35000.0,
    elements_per_gb: float = 1.0e6,
    memory_safety_factor: float = 0.90
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Evaluates a Laghos run and provides a high-level decision and strategic hint.

    This function acts as a "diagnostician" by analyzing the performance of a
    completed Laghos run against a theoretical model. It identifies the most
    likely bottleneck (memory, poor scaling, or hardware underutilization) and
    returns a machine-readable strategic hint for what to try next.

    Args:
        total_elements (int): The total number of mesh elements in the simulation.
        total_ranks (int): The total number of MPI tasks used for the run.
        nodes_used (int): The number of compute nodes used for the run.
        cores_per_node (int): The number of physical CPU cores on a single compute node.
        memory_gb_per_node (int): The total system RAM in Gigabytes on a single compute node.
        threading_hint (int): Specifies the SMT/Hyper-Threading level to assume (e.g., 1 for no SMT, 2 for SMT).
        current_fom (float): The measured performance from the run, typically in FOM/second.
        threshold (float): The performance goal, as a fraction of the theoretical maximum (default 0.90).
        ideal_fom_per_core (float): A tuning constant for the max FOM of a single core (default 1.5e6 FOM/sec).
        efficiency_sweet_spot (float): A tuning constant for elements/rank needed for ~76% efficiency (default 35,000).
        elements_per_gb (float): A tuning constant for the memory model (elements per GB of RAM, default 1.0e6).
        memory_safety_factor (float): A safety margin for memory usage (default 0.90).

    Returns:
        (dict): A dictionary containing 'decision', 'reason', 'strategy_hint', and 'metrics'.
    """
    if total_ranks == 0:
        return {"decision": "RETRY", "reason": "The number of tasks cannot be zero.", "strategy_hint": "INCREASE_TASKS"}

    # --- Calculate Theoretical Performance and Ratios ---
    elements_per_rank = total_elements / total_ranks
    max_cores_on_node = cores_per_node * threading_hint
    cores_per_rank = max_cores_on_node // total_ranks if nodes_used == 1 else cores_per_node
    total_cores_used = total_ranks * cores_per_rank
    
    scaling_efficiency = math.tanh(elements_per_rank / efficiency_sweet_spot)
    effective_fom_per_core = ideal_fom_per_core * scaling_efficiency
    theoretical_max_fom = effective_fom_per_core * total_cores_used

    performance_ratio = 0.0
    if theoretical_max_fom > 1e-9:
        performance_ratio = current_fom / theoretical_max_fom

    estimated_memory_gb = total_elements / elements_per_gb
    memory_utilization = estimated_memory_gb / (memory_gb_per_node * nodes_used) if nodes_used > 0 else 0
    
    metrics = {
        "performance_ratio": round(performance_ratio, 3),
        "scaling_efficiency": round(scaling_efficiency, 3),
        "memory_utilization": round(memory_utilization, 3),
        "elements_per_rank": int(elements_per_rank),
        "theoretical_max_fom_per_sec": f"{theoretical_max_fom:.2e}"
    }

    # --- Decision Logic based on prioritized bottlenecks ---
    
    if performance_ratio >= threshold:
        return {
            "decision": "STOP",
            "reason": f"Optimization goal reached. Current performance is at {performance_ratio:.1%} of the theoretical maximum, meeting the {threshold:.1%} threshold.",
            "metrics": metrics
        }
    
    if memory_utilization >= memory_safety_factor:
        return {
            "decision": "RETRY",
            "reason": f"Memory utilization is critically high at {memory_utilization:.1%}. The number of elements is too large for the allocated memory.",
            "strategy_hint": "DECREASE_ELEMENTS",
            "metrics": metrics
        }

    if scaling_efficiency < 0.5: # Heuristic for "low" efficiency
         return {
            "decision": "RETRY",
            "reason": f"Scaling efficiency is low ({scaling_efficiency:.1%}), indicating the number of elements per rank is too small (communication-bound).",
            "strategy_hint": "INCREASE_ELEMENTS",
            "metrics": metrics
        }
    
    if nodes_used == 1 and total_ranks < max_cores_on_node:
        return {
            "decision": "RETRY",
            "reason": f"The node is under-subscribed ({total_ranks}/{max_cores_on_node} tasks used). Hardware is not fully utilized.",
            "strategy_hint": "INCREASE_TASKS",
            "metrics": metrics
        }

    return {
        "decision": "RETRY",
        "reason": f"Performance is at {performance_ratio:.1%} of theoretical max, which is below the {threshold:.1%} threshold. Current configuration is reasonable but can be improved.",
        "strategy_hint": "INCREASE_ELEMENTS",
        "metrics": metrics
    }
